pageCache.pageTitle: St. Joseph's School & Nursery | Malmesbury - Home
pageCache.text:
Broad, Creative, Ambitious
Welcome to St Joseph's School & Nursery, nestled in the ancient Cotswold town of Malmesbury.
A village school, in the heart of Malmesbury
Academic Ambition
Experience our new curriculum from September 2026 - inspired by classical 'liberal arts' - to challenge and inspire children, and provide a strong foundation for personal growth and future success.
Enriching Extracurricular
Explore a diverse range of after school clubs that enrich children's learning. From Italian Club, to Netball, Art, Board Games and Choir, our offering fosters personal development, creativity, and teamwork.
Nursery to Year 6
St Joseph's boasts a state-of-the-art Nursery School for children aged from 2 years. We provide continuity of education until the end of Year 6 (ages 2- 11).
Welcome to St. Joseph’s School & Nursery
St. Joseph’s is an ambitious school where the children are given the opportunity to flourish, first and foremost, as human beings.
We offer a small-scale, personalised learning environment, where every child is known.
The school was founded in 1868 and moved to its current site in Malmesbury in 1932. It’s got the feeling of a village school, yet is only a stone’s throw from the heart of the town centre with its historic market, cafes and beautiful, Romanesque Abbey.
Alongside high academic aspirations, modern ‘millennial’ parents (of which I am one) are seeking out schools which educate the whole person and nurture creativity, cultivate social awareness and give opportunities for collaboration.
St Joseph’s children are happy in heart, mind and spirit.
I hope you’ll come and see us.
Visit us
St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School HollowayMalmesburyWiltshire SN16 9BB
Telephone: 01666 822331Email: admin@sjpschool.co.uk

At St Joseph’s, we have six virtues, underpinned by the principle of the Golden Rule: “Do to others that you would have them do to you” (Matthew 7:12).
These underpin the actions of St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School and are a gift we want to give all pupils.
The virtues aim to deepen children’s understanding of the wider virtues Jesus shared. They are:
Our aspiration is that through these all children will become the best versions of themselves, now and for the rest of their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music & Drama - St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music & Drama
In addition to weekly class music lessons, where children make music using tuned and untuned percussion, there are opportunities to learn the piano, singing, violin and recorder.
St Joseph’s has worked with professional violinist Michael Bochmann MBE and his charity Water City Music for the last few years, and last year pianists took part in a concert in Malmesbury Abbey alongside another primary school in a concert designed to inspire the next generation of musicians.
There are regular recitals in the School Hall for parents throughout the year.
Children at St Joseph’s love to sing!
Children learn a wide repertoire of hymns ranging from traditional to contemporary and they enjoy a weekly singing assembly on Wednesday afternoons.
Choir meets every Wednesday lunchtime and is free to KS 2 children. They perform at many community events throughout the year.
In 2025, these included Stand Up to Cancer fundraising afternoon, Malmesbury’s Late Night Shopping Event and Heals’s Christmas lunch. The choir regularly entertain in residential homes and support local celebrations such as St Aldhelm’s 150th anniversary.
St Joseph’s children performed the musical Oh! Athelstan in Malmesbury Abbey, written by John Hughes and Mike Scanlon, as part of the town’s celebration of Athelstan 1100 and also sang in the opening ceremony.
St Joseph’s students love a good musical! The whole school performed the professional version of Joseph and the Amazing Technicolour Dreamcoat to a packed out Abbey last July. This year we are rehearsing Hannah and the Tyger, another musical by John Hughes and Mike Scanlon. This was only performed once before in 2006 and we are very proud to be able to perform it, putting our St Joseph’s spin on it, and including every child in the primary school.
Every year, the school performs a Nativity Play for parents.
2026 Production: Hannah & the Tyger
Following their sell-out performance of Joseph! the cast of St. Joseph’s School & Nursery returned with a ground-breaking production of Hannah and the Tyger.
The year was 1703, and a young barmaid, Hannah Twynnoy, could not resist the temptation of stroking a tiger from a visiting circus. What happened next made for the greatest unsolved mystery of Malmesbury.
Written by local artistic powerhouse, John Hughes and Mike Scanlon, 80 childnre, aged 4-11, played to a packed audience in Malmesbury Abbey.

pageCache.pageTitle: Phonics & Early Reading - St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Phonics & Early Reading
We use Unlocking Letters and Sounds which was validated by the DfE in December 2021.
We begin teaching phonics in the first few weeks of term 1 in Reception and children make rapid progress in their reading journey. Children begin to learn the main sounds heard in the English Language and how they can be represented, as well as learning ‘Common Exception’ words for Phases 2, 3 and 4. They use these sounds to read and write simple words, captions and sentences. Children leave Reception being able to apply the phonemes taught within Phase 2, 3 and 4.
https://www.st-josephs-malmesbury.wilts.sch.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Actions-for-phase-2.docx
In Year 1 through Phase 5a, b and c, they learn any alternative spellings and pronunciations for the graphemes and additional Common Exception Words. By the end of Year 1 children will have mastered using phonics to decode and blend when reading and segment when spelling. In Year 1 all children are screened using the national Phonics Screening Check. In Year 2, phonics continues to be revisited to ensure mastery of the phonetic code and any child who does not meet age related expectations will continue to receive support to close identified gaps.
For further details please see the Unlocking Letters and Sounds progression: https://www.st-josephs-malmesbury.wilts.sch.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/ULS-Summary-progression.docx
To ensure no child is left behind at any point in the progression, children are regularly assessed and supported to keep up through bespoke 1-1 interventions. These include GPC recognition and blending and segmenting interventions. The lowest attaining 20% of pupils are closely monitored to ensure these interventions have an impact.
Early Reading Scheme
At St Joseph’s we promote a ‘phonics first’ approach and in both our guided reading sessions at school and in the books children take home, texts are very closely matched to a child’s current phonics knowledge so that every child can experience real success in their reading. In these crucial early stages of reading we primarily use books from Ransom Reading Stars Phonics, to ensure complete fidelity to the Unlocking Letters and Sounds progression we follow.
Once children progress beyond decodable texts, they move onto our book scheme so that they can continue to progress in their decoding, fluency and comprehension skills to become avid, expert readers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum - St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
At St Joseph’s, we provide a broad, balanced, creative and ambitious curriculum, which ensures our children are prepared for the next stages of their education and lives.
Our curriculum provides our pupils with the essential core knowledge and skills as directed by the National Curriculum. We aim to provide a curriculum which is enriching and challenging, where children experience the opportunity to learn in a wide range of contexts.
A Liberal Arts Approach
Our pedagogical outlook is also influenced by ‘liberal arts’ curricula, which help children to encounter ‘the best that has been known and said’. Through our weekly enrichment sessions, we want to help children learn by making connections. A firm grasp of Maths and English in the early years underpins our aspiration for a high degree of cultural literacy further up the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEN & Inclusion - St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
SEN & Inclusion
At St Joseph’s we celebrate and welcome that all children are unique and have different ways of learning, playing and communicating. Some children have additional needs and need some extra support with their education. As the SEND Code of Practice (2015) states “All children and young people are entitled to an education that enables them to make progress so that they achieve their best, become confident individuals living fulfilling lives, and make a successful transition into adulthood.”
St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School is a small, inclusive and nurturing school where we strive to ensure that all of our children, regardless of need and ability, are able to thrive and become inquisitive and ambitious learners. We balance support and aspiration, ensuring that our high expectations are shared by all. As stated in our SEND Policy ‘We recognise that all children have the right to an inclusive, broad, balanced and meaningful curriculum including extra-curricular activities where appropriate, and full access to the National Curriculum.’
We support our children with additional needs through a wide range of strategies, both learning focused and holistic. Please see our School Information Report (SIR) Sept 2025, below, for details on the interventions and strategies that we use, how we adapt teaching and learning to meet the needs of all our children and how we identify needs.
We are proud of our extensive ‘Universal’ offer, that is, the high quality teaching and support that is available in every classroom to all children. As well as our Universal offer, our bespoke Ordinarily Available Provision (OAP) Map also documents our Targeted and Specialist support available to those with additional needs.
Other key documents:
SEND Annual report to Governors and Parents 2024/25
SEND Policy Sept 2025
SEND in a Nutshell Sept 2025
SEND Information Report
Our SENCo is Mrs Sharon Carpenter and she is always happy to talk to you about the provision that we offer:
Phone: 01666 822331 Email: senco@sjpschool.co.uk
Mrs Carpenter is supported by the SEN Governor, Mrs Carole Baker.
Our ELSA TA is Mrs Hanna Webb and our Parent Support Advisor is Mrs Terry Jones.
Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing
Through our nurturing, family-feel ethos, we endeavour to ensure each and every pupil, family and member of staff is valued and feels safe. We aim to develop the emotional wellbeing of our children, and promote their learning about being both physically and mentally healthy, in line with the DfE guidance: Promoting Children and Young People’s Mental Health and Wellbeing 2021. We aim to identify early signs that help is required and support families with this in school as well as signposting to outside agencies.
Our school mental health provision is greatly supported by Mrs Webb and Mrs Jones. Mrs Hanna Webb is our Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA) and our Parent Support Adviser (PSA) is Mrs Terry Jones. You can contact both through the school office.
Sometimes, our young people have to support with caring for others in their family who may have medical, social and emotional or physical needs. This can bring many challenges that families may need support with. The organisations below offer excellent support for Young Carers and you may wish to make contact with them if this applies to you. A Young Carer can also be a child who simply lives with a sibling or parent whose additional needs impact upon family dynamics and activities.
https://www.wiltshire.gov.uk/children-young-people-young-carers
https://www.communityfirst.org.uk/yaw/young-carers/
We are privileged to be a diverse school and have families whose home languages include Spanish, Shona, Bengali, Polish and Bulgarian! Some of these children are already, or very quickly, become proficient in English when they start with us but for others, having to learn and socialise in a new and unfamiliar language can be a barrier. We work alongside the excellent team at the Wiltshire Ethnic Minority and Traveller Achievement Service – EMTAS – to support those of our children who are on the pathway to learning English.
We also ensure that we support parents and carers whose first language is not English, by, for example, translating important information and having conversations face to face rather than over the ‘phone, with translators if needed
https://family-action.org.uk/services/wiltshire-sendiass/
https://www.wiltshire.gov.uk/article/9954/SEND-Advice-and-Information

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School - St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Learning Outdoors
Outdoor learning is central to the curriculum at St. Joseph’s.
Children from Nursery to Year 6 benefit from our brand new Forest School Shelter, Nature Classroom and historic, riverside grounds.
The children will be given the opportunity to take part in a wide variety of activities using the natural resources available to them. Some (but not limited to) of the possible activities are listed below:
Plant and tree identification
Vegetable growing
Mini-beast identification
Shelter building
Using tools
Creating natural artwork
Coppicing
Woodland management
Fire lighting
Climbing
Outdoor games
Why Outdoors?
Outdoor learning has been in vogue for some time now, but one of the biggest surprises about St Joseph’s is that it is set on a larger estate in which the children can take advantage of ‘welly walks’, pond-dipping and a much-loved forest school.
The importance of fresh air and learning outdoors has been well documented.
Outdoor learning improves physical health, boosts cognitive development, increases concentration, creativity and problem-solving skills.
Children build resilience, self-confidence and a deeper connection with nature.

Pupil Premium - St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
The Government allocates an amount of money to schools to support the most vulnerable children. This is known as Pupil Premium funding. The Government states ‘additional funding is given to publicly funded schools in England to raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils and close the gap between them and their peers.’ At St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School, we believe that all children have the right to a quality education which includes a range of experiences. We aim to close the disadvantage gap by addressing inequalities and raising the attainment of those students in low-income families. A premium has also been introduced for children whose parents are currently serving in the armed forces. This service premium is designed to address the emotional and social well being of these pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: RE - St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
As a Catholic school, our aim is to provide a caring community in which each child has opportunities to deepen their understanding of the Catholic faith and learn and immerse themselves in the fundamentals of Christian belief and teaching.
In partnership with home and parish, we want all within our community to show love and kindness to one and other in their thoughts, words and actions.
Our Religious Education curriculum is designed to be:
Children have opportunities to develop as independent, resilient, confident and successful learners.
Through the “Learning from” element of every lesson, children are challenged to develop high aspirations and be guided through discussion and reflection to know how they can make a positive contribution to their class, school, community and wider society.
There is a high focus on developing children’s moral, spiritual, social and cultural understanding through “Hearing” , “Believing”, “Celebrating” and “Living” through the knowledge and experiences they gain from our curriculum, other faiths, cultures and backgrounds.
Religious Education is a core subject which is taught for 10% of school’s time tabled week.
To support us in the delivery of RE we follow the Catholic Education Service, Religious Education Directory “To know you more clearly” programme of study so that this meets the diocesan standards for primary Religious Education. We use the Clifton Diocese planning and resources for each topic theme.
We integrate elements of Catholic Social Teaching into our own progression of content and deeply root our school virtue themes into this yearly progression.
Our lessons provide opportunities for celebration, prayer and reflection. Children are taught about God’s love and their Christian responsibility.
There is a high focus on developing children’s moral, spiritual, social and cultural understanding through “Hearing” , “Believing”, “Celebrating” and “Living” through the knowledge and experiences they gain from our curriculum.
Our progressive journey through the curriculum gives children the language of religious experience through activities, stories, symbols, rituals and celebration. It promotes core Gospel values which underpin all aspects of school life.
The children are encouraged to make links with their own experiences and through this explore and explain their own beliefs and values.
The theme for Term 2 is Prophesy and Promise.
We celebrate equality and diversity supporting the children’s social and cultural development, recognising every individual as special and unique in the image and likeness of God. Through this, children are encouraged to also be respectful of and understand the people and traditions linked to other faiths, cultures and backgrounds.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Joseph’s Nursery School - St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
St Joseph’s Nursery School
Welcome!Our brand new Nursery School opened in September 2025.
We offer continuity of education to our children from ages 2-11 (Nursery – Year 6). Most children who attend the nursery continue Reception, but we welcome all children who would like to attend.
Nursery children benefit from all the facilities of the main school, including:
Child-centered pedagogy
Children in the Nursery are supported by staff with experience of Early Years and Key Stage 1, so we can adapt to each child’s individual learning needs.
We have specialist staff who work across the school supporting children’s special educational needs (SEND), Speech and Language (S&L) and wider emotional development. This includes Emotional Literacy Support (ELSA) and playing therapies.
The Nursery School benefits from our whole-school provision.
School integration and firm friendships
Starting school is a big deal!
At St. Joseph’s, the transition from Nursery to Reception is seamless. Children (and their parents!) stay settled as they make their important step into school life.
Moving into Reception feels natural, as the children keep close friends, teachers and support staff who know them really well, as individuals. Familiarity with the routines of the school day builds confidence and allows St Joseph’s children to start their school journey with optimism and certainty.
At St Joseph’s, friendships are not artificially limited to year groups (like larger primary schools). Children in tutor groups further up love to visit the Nursery – and are often to be found reading to the littlest members of the school during their breaktime!
Please use the following documents to apply for a place in St Joseph’s Nursery.
The link to Childcare Choices will provide parents with the most up to date information on accessing 15 and 30 hour funding and is important in helping parents understand how to make nursery applications.
Hot, home-cooked lunches

Nursery Application Sept 2025

Our purpose-built early years classroom provides a bespoke learning space that is designed specifically for nursery-aged children, including separate toilet and changing facilities along with a mini kitchen area.
Children also have direct access to an outdoor learning area, shared with our EYFS & Key Stage 1 class. This includes a mud kitchen, role play areas and play equipment designed to help children balance and hold their own weight.
Come and see for yourself! Email or call to arrange a tour of our inspiring setting:
